title: Scienter liability historically concerns harm caused by an animal where the keeper knew of a dangerous propensity and failed to control it

content.overview: Scienter liability historically concerns harm caused by an animal where the keeper knew of a dangerous propensity and failed to control it. Modern Indian claims must also be tested against negligence and applicable animal-control statutes.
content.glance: Scienter liability historically concerns harm caused by an animal where the keeper knew of a dangerous propensity and failed to control it. Modern Indian claims must also be tested against negligence and applicable animal-control statutes.
content.study: Scienter liability historically concerns harm caused by an animal where the keeper knew of a dangerous propensity and failed to control it. Modern Indian claims must also be tested against negligence and applicable animal-control statutes.\n\nThe common-law scienter action distinguishes ordinary animal behaviour from a known vicious or dangerous tendency. Knowledge is central. Indian courts may apply common-law principles where consistent with Indian law, while negligence may provide a separate route where the keeper failed to take reasonable care.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: The common-law scienter action distinguishes ordinary animal behaviour from a known vicious or dangerous tendency. Knowledge is central. Indian courts may apply common-law principles where consistent with Indian law, while negligence may provide a separate route where the keeper failed to take reasonable care.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: The doctrine is not a comprehensive Indian statutory code. The claimant should plead keeper responsibility, dangerous propensity, knowledge, causal injury and absence of a defeating defence or statutory allocation.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Defendant is the keeper or legally responsible person. 2. Animal has a dangerous propensity relevant to the injury. 3. Defendant knows of that propensity. 4. Animal causes the harm. 5. No applicable defence defeats liability.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: Prior attacks, warnings, complaints, veterinary records and admissions may prove knowledge. Mere ownership does not by itself establish scienter liability. The claimant must connect the known tendency to the injury.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Plead the animal's conduct, prior knowledge and causal injury. If local statutory duties apply, identify them first. Limitation follows the applicable cause of action and statute.

examples.title: Illustration 1 — Doctrine Satisfied
examples.body: Knowledge of dangerous propensity is central to the historical scienter action; negligence may be pleaded alternatively where appropriate. The claimant must still prove the remaining ingredients on the civil standard.

examples.title: Illustration 2 — Boundary Defect
examples.body: The historical scienter doctrine has specific ingredients and modern claims may instead or additionally depend on negligence or statute. A court should not infer liability from the label alone.
